newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - March 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - March 5.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on March 5. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

State Secretary Murdiono said President Suharto's recent statement that he would "clobber" anybody who tried to unseat him through unconstitutional means should serve as a warning to potential lawbreakers.
Finance Minister Mar'ie Muhammad said the government would not hesitate to liquidate ailing banks to strengthen the banking industry in the face of financial liberation in Asia.
Southeast Asian cocoa producers have discussed the possibility of establishing a common regional trading contract as an alternative to the existing contracts of London, New York and Paris.

Finance Minister Mar'ie Muhammad said Indonesia's 1996/97 (April-March) budget is expected to show a surplus of 817.9 billion rupiah. He said the 1996/97 budget revenue stands at 95.840 trillion rupiah with expenditure expected to reach 95.022 trillion rupiah.

The government will not review rules on campaign for the May 29 general elections despite protests from the Moslem-based United Development Party (PPP), one of the three contestants in the general elections. The PPP has complained that the rules were too restrictive.
